title: Interaction Thermostat — lightweight per-route fidelity controller (PRD draft)
body:
High-level idea:
A lightweight, first-class control primitive (nicknamed 'Interaction Thermostat') that lets product teams tune response fidelity/cost/latency for a given route, user cohort, or API key using a single continuous knob. Think: user-facing "thermostat" for inference quality — set point determines how aggressively we apply batching, KV caching, quantization, and fallback routing.

Why this? (problem statement)
- Teams repeatedly re-create ad-hoc fidelity lanes (cheap vs premium) with brittle feature flags and many duplicate code paths.
- We need a simple, observable, and SDK-friendly way to trade cost vs quality per route without changing prompts.
- Current rollout paths (A/B + model variants) are heavy; operators want a single control that surfaces unit-econ impact.

What the Thermostat should do (initial scope)
- Expose a continuous numeric setting (0.0..1.0) per API route / API key / user segment where 0 = minimal cost (aggressive batching, prefer quantized variant, short cache TTLs) and 1 = max fidelity (larger token budgets, full precision model variant, relaxed batching).
- Map the numeric value to a deterministic policy that changes: model variant selection, quantization level, cache TTL/prefixing aggressiveness, max-response-length, request timeouts, and preferred region routing.
- Provide SDK+REST hooks: route-level config via Console, and a runtime header override (x-rw-thermostat:0.7) for dev testing.
- Runtime should emit telemetry: chosen policy name, estimated per-token cost delta, latency impact, and a quality proxy score (existing eval ping).

User stories
- As a growth PM I want to open the Console and set the chat route for the free tier to thermostat 0.25 so we reduce cost for anonymous users without changing prompts.
- As an SRE I want the thermostat to automatically nudge down for the route when 95th p90 latency > SLO to maintain availability.
- As an engineer I want a local SDK flag to simulate thermostat=0.9 so I can validate UX regression before release.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Console: per-route thermostat slider persisted and versioned.
- API: runtime honors header override and resolves a policy with deterministic precedence (header > api_key > route default).
- Serving runtime: maps policy to at least these knobs: model_variant, quantization_profile, batch_priority, cache_ttl.
- Telemetry: every request logs resolved thermostat value and the resulting policy tags; costs & latencies surfaced in per-route dashboard.
- Docs: quickstart and recommended default mappings for common workloads.

Experiment matrix (how we validate)
- A/B on two cohorts for a mid-sized customer: control=thermostat 1.0 (current prod), treatment=0.4. Metrics: tokens per session, p50/p95 latency, user engagement (task completion), model quality regression via automated evals.
- Canary safety: auto-fallback to parent policy when error rate spikes > 3x baseline.

Implementation notes / mapping sketch (rough)
- Thermostat value -> policy buckets: 0.0-0.2 = "frugal", 0.2-0.6 = "balanced", 0.6-1.0 = "fidelity".
- Policy config file (console-backed) has per-bucket overrides: preferred_model, fallback_chain, quant_profile, cache_ttl_ms, batch_priority_class, max_tokens.
- Runtime resolution: (1) check x-rw-thermostat header; (2) check api_key override; (3) route default; (4) global default (0.6). Resolve to bucket and apply policy.
- Safety layer: each policy includes "min_quality_checks": a lightweight eval that runs on a tiny sample (local replay) before enabling a new mapping in prod.

Console / UX ideas
- Slider with three quick presets + numeric input.
- Per-route historical view showing tokens/sec, cost delta vs baseline, and a small quality regression sparkline (from evals).
- "Simulate" mode to replay last 100 requests and show what would have changed.

Metrics / telemetry to track
- Per-route: avg thermostat, tokens/session, tokens/request, cost per 1k requests, p50/p95 latency, error rate, eval-quality-delta.
- Global: percent of traffic in each bucket, cost savings vs baseline, number of auto-adjust events from SRE rules.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0: design + policy-to-runtime mapping prototype (internal).
- Phase 1: SDK header, basic runtime mapping, telemetry. Pilot with 2-3 internal teams.
- Phase 2: Console controls, canary experiments, auto-adjust SRE rules.
- Phase 3: GA + docs + suggested templates for common use cases.

Open questions / risks
- How to measure "quality" cheaply enough to auto-adjust? Need a small eval harness tied to production prompts (privacy concerns).
- Interaction with existing Dedicated/Private deployments — need to surface which knobs are legal in Private (e.g., not forcing quantization without explicit consent).
- Billing model: show estimated cost delta but do we bill differently? (probably not initially, but expose visibility).

Follow-ups / next ideas (parking)
- "Thermostat profiles": save+share preset profiles per org (e.g., education, e-commerce).
- Per-user adaptive thermostat: use engagement signals to raise fidelity during conversion flows.
- Combine with rollout manifold so thermostat value can be part of canary configs.

Notes to self (to do)
- Wire up a tiny mock in the local dev runtime to test header override.
- Sync with Mika (eval infra) on a minimal quality proxy for canary gating.
- Draft a short Console prototype flow and collect feedback from Solutions Eng.

References / context
- Related internal docs: TOKEN-BUDGETING playbook, session-econ sketches (see linked artifacts).
- Competitive: a few competitors have lane-based toggles; our diff is continuous knob + strong telemetry and SDK override.

Rough timeline target: 8–10 weeks to pilot with internal teams if we prioritize (fast prototype + telemetry first).

-- end of notes --

(Informal: this is a jam dump — goal is to get developer-facing control that feels simple. Keep it lightweight and observable. Will iterate after first sync with Eval + Runtime.)
